subject: SLA template negotiation: uptime floor, credits, and maintenance carveouts
messages:
From: Julia Singh <julia.singh@opticore.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Aug 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline and maintenance carveouts

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — OptiCore’s platform team is excited about the latency numbers, but procurement has a few hard requirements we need captured in the contract before we can move to PO. High level:

- We need a written availability commitment that covers both interactive routes (low-latency) and batched inference workloads. Ideally 99.98% monthly uptime for interactive endpoints; batched jobs can tolerate lower availability but must not affect our SLAs.
- Monthly service credit scheme that scales with impact; we’re looking for a cap that allows us to recover meaningful amounts when incidents materially affect production (we typically ask for up to ~30% of the monthly invoice in extreme months).
- Scheduled maintenance must be excluded from uptime calculations but only with advance notice. Standard ask is 48 hours notice and a clear monthly maintenance window allowance.

Can you send your SLA template + any flex points around credits, maintenance carveouts, and latency-based SLOs? Our procurement timeline aims to finish redlines by next Friday (2024-09-06).

Also attaching a short CSV with our batched inference footprint to help your SREs understand peak patterns (see attached).

Best,
Julia Singh
Head of Procurement, OptiCore
procurement@opticore.com

Attachment: opticore-batched-inference-footprint.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Singh <julia.singh@opticore.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Aug 2024 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and maintenance carveouts

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear ask and the footprint file, that helps. Attaching our standard SLA template (redwood-sla-proposal-v2.pdf) and a short note below on flex points.

Quick summary: our default hosted SLA is 99.95% monthly availability (measured at the customer-facing route layer) with a service-credit formula tied to minutes of unplanned downtime; the maximum monthly credit is 25% of the invoice for that billing period. Scheduled maintenance windows are excluded from availability when we provide >=72 hours advance notice and limit total monthly maintenance to 4 hours per region.

Flex points we can consider for OptiCore:
- Interactive endpoints: we can offer a targeted 99.98% availability objective for reserved interactive capacity (requires Dedicated or pinned capacity) — this is an "objective" that triggers faster paging and a higher-priority remediation path, not a wholesale raise of the hosted SLA baseline.
- Credit cap: we are willing to bridge to a 30% cap for the first 90 days following go-live as a ramp; after that the standard 25% cap applies.
- Maintenance notice: we can shorten to 48h notice for non-impactful patches if agreed in advance, but for major scheduled maintenance we prefer 72h.
- Batching carveout: we can exclude backfilled/batch job windows from availability if the batch jobs run on a clearly identified route and are pinned to burst capacity — we do not exclude batched jobs that share interactive routing.

I’ve copied Aditya (product) for any technical constraints and to start an internal note if OptiCore is pushing for a firm 99.98% baseline. If you’re happy with the ramp-to-30% approach plus the interactive objective, we can produce a revised redline for legal and a DocuSign link.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-v2.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

Date: Fri, 30 Aug 2024 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and maintenance carveouts

Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposal. A few follow-ups from our side after internal review:

1) Interactive baseline: OptiCore’s risk model is centered on a 99.98% uptime floor across production routes handling customer-facing requests. We understand Redwood’s separation of "objective" vs baseline, but we need contractual language that commits to the 99.98% floor for interactive routes used by our customers (we can map routes to a service namespace).

2) Credit cap: given our exposure, we’d like the monthly cap at 35% for months where impact exceeds a defined threshold (we propose the threshold at >120 aggregated minutes of unplanned downtime). If Redwood cannot accept 35% across the board, we will accept 30% as a minimum.

3) Maintenance notification: 48h notice is preferred for planning and we require a rolling monthly summary of actual maintenance performed and associated windows.

We’re constrained to finalize redlines by next Friday — can you confirm whether Redwood can accept either (A) 99.98% interactive baseline + 30% initial cap or (B) 99.95% baseline + 35% cap? Option A is our preference.

Thanks,
Julia

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Sep 2024 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fw: SLA baseline and maintenance carveouts — OptiCore counterproposal

Folks — forwarding OptiCore’s counter (below). Quick summary and recommended positions before legal starts redlines: 

- OptiCore prefers 99.98% firm baseline for interactive routes (they asked to map routes to a namespace). I recommend we hold firm that the hosted baseline remains 99.95% and offer 99.98% as a contractual objective applicable only to reserved/pinned interactive capacity (Dedicated). Rationale: engineering can meet the objective with pinned capacity guarantees and different remediation prioritization.
- Credit cap: they ask 35% or at least 30%. I think we can accept 30% for first 90 days (commercial concession) and keep 25% standard after the ramp; 35% is too open-ended for us without additional protections (e.g., defining severity bands and remediation timelines).
- Maintenance: they want 48h + monthly summary. We can agree to 48h for non-major patches and commit to a monthly maintenance log. For major maintenance maintain 72h.

Connor — can you draft redlines that: (1) tie the 99.98% objective to a named service namespace and Dedicated capacity; (2) implement a temporary 30% cap for first 90 days post-go-live, then 25%; (3) add the monthly maintenance summary deliverable and a notification window matrix.

I’m happy to be on the thread with OptiCore for clarifications once you have a draft.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Singh <julia.singh@opticore.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Sep 2024 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and maintenance carveouts — proposed compromise

Hi Julia — thanks for the clarity and for surfacing the priority items. We ran this with product and legal and below is a proposed compromise that we believe addresses OptiCore’s concerns while keeping operational guardrails that work for our SREs.

Summary of proposal (compromise):
- Baseline: Redwood hosted baseline remains 99.95% monthly availability for the general service.
- Interactive guarantee (contractual): For interactive routes that OptiCore maps to the named service namespace and that are pinned to Dedicated (reserved) capacity, Redwood will include a contractual guarantee of 99.98% monthly availability for the first 6 months following go-live. This guarantee is limited to requests routed via the named namespace and only while the Dedicated reservation is active.
- Credits: Redwood will increase the monthly credit cap to 30% of the invoice for the first 90 days post-go-live as a commercial ramp. After 90 days the cap reverts to the standard 25%. Credits continue to be calculated per the SLA formula in the attached PDF.
- Maintenance: We will provide a rolling monthly maintenance summary (dates, windows, impacted namespaces) and agree to 48h notice for non-major patches and 72h for major scheduled maintenance. Emergency maintenance remains excluded but will be accompanied by a post-incident report within 72h.

Next steps: I’ve attached the revised SLA redline and created a DocuSign envelope for signature (link below). If this looks acceptable I can issue a DocuSign and loop in finance for PO instructions.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC123456789
Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-v2-revised.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

Please confirm by EOD Wednesday 2024-09-04 if you can accept this compromise (we’ll be ready to route redlines to legal if you need tweaks).

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
